newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. Aetna planning India joint venture.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Aetna planning India joint venture.

text.p: U.S. insurance giant Aetna Inc said on Wednesday it is in talks with prospective Indian partners to set up a joint venture company with an initial investment of at least $25 million.
"In this market, we have decided we should have a joint venture," said Frederick Copeland, president and chief executive officer of Aetna International Inc, the company's international arm.

"We would start out small and we would gradually build on that. We would hope our starting point would be capitalising a company in the $25 million to $40 million range, but there is no limit," Copeland told a news conference in the Indian capital.
The Indian government has agreed to set up an insurance regulatory body in anticipation of an eventual end to the state monopoly but has yet to allow foreign investment into the sector.
Copeland said he was discussing Aetna's plans with a number of Indian companies, and could consider a state-owned insurance firm as a possible partner. He gave no other details.
The new company would provide life insurance, health care and pension services, he said.
"India is very attractive because insurance premiums are very low relative to GDP and potential GDP," Copeland said, referring to gross domestic product.
"We are now examining all aspects of what it would take to be a productive player in the marketplace."
